notes: Searches shared pool: 22 combined across the three items; ~12 relevant to sildenafil. Doubts: (1) 999/A&E for prolonged erection stated on one NHS page and UCLH; other NHS/SmPC wording is 'immediate medical assistance' and hour thresholds differ (2, 3-4, 4 hours), so no hours given; consider reviewing against the live NHS sildenafil side-effects page. (2) UK regulatory: prescription is the default; Viagra Connect tablets are a pharmacy medicine (MHRA/GOV.UK, 2018), added as a second UK regulatory entry - check the compiler accepts two UK entries. (3) Revatio/Grandipam named by NHS about page via search summary; Revatio was not otherwise retrieved. (4) Pregnancy/breastfeeding: NHS pregnancy page is mostly written for pulmonary hypertension use; breastfeeding sentence removed. (5) Grapefruit and alpha-blocker caution rest on SmPC/PMC (class-wide), not an NHS sildenafil page. (6) Formulary-based optic-nerve sentence comes from a local formulary document. (7) 'Not usually used in pregnancy' is for erection problems only. (8) Dissolvable tablets unconfirmed, omitted.
